blocks.text: Quality Power Electrical Equipments (QPEEL) is a Sangli-based holding company for a group of high-voltage equipment businesses. [F] (AR2025 p.4) The parent makes air-core and iron-core reactors (coil products), line traps and medium-voltage transformers used in HVDC converter stations, FACTS installations and AC substations. Mehru (51%, Bhiwadi) makes instrument transformers up to 500kV. Endoks (51%, Ankara) builds turnkey FACTS systems (SVC, STATCOM), automation and battery-storage power conversion systems (PCS). [F] (AR2025 p.4) [F] (AR2025 p.171) It earns money by selling custom-engineered equipment against fixed-price purchase orders, mostly to system integrators and EPC contractors (Hitachi, Siemens, GE, Schneider, Hyosung) and to utilities and renewable developers. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

**The consolidated group is mostly the subsidiaries, not the listed parent.** In FY25, Endoks contributed Rs 65.0 cr of the Rs 100.1 cr consolidated PAT (65%), and the standalone parent contributed Rs 30.3 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.218) For FY26, management gives the revenue split as QP (parent plus projects arm) about Rs 246 cr, Mehru Rs 318 cr and Endoks Rs 468 cr. [MC] (CALL May 2026) That split adds to about Rs 1,032 cr [E]. It does not reconcile with the Rs 947 cr consolidated sales in our statements data. [F] (NUMBERS) Both Mehru and Endoks are 51% owned, so a large share of group profit belongs to minority holders. FY25 profit attributable to non-controlling interests was Rs 34.0 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.166)

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. The price needs growth the business has never shown organically. The reverse DCF implies 87.8% sales CAGR for five years against a base-case equivalent of 19.8%. [F] (NUMBERS) The bull scenario's per-share value is Rs 356.4 against a Rs 1,585 price. [F] (NUMBERS)

2. Minorities take a large share of the profits. Endoks and Mehru are 51% subsidiaries. [F] (AR2025 p.171) FY25 NCI took Rs 34.0 cr of Rs 100.1 cr PAT. [F] (AR2025 p.166) The 62.9x trailing P/E in our data is market cap over total PAT of Rs 195 cr, while TTM EPS is Rs 17.21. [F] (NUMBERS) The per-share multiple is therefore materially higher than the headline. [AI]
3. Cash conversion is weak. CFO was 0.43x PAT in FY26 and 0.55x over three years, and FY26 FCF was negative Rs 31 cr. [F] (NUMBERS)

4. Other income is a big share of profit, and some of it is hyperinflation accounting. Other income was 27% of FY26 PBT. [F] (NUMBERS) FY25 other income included a Rs 12.8 cr net monetary gain. [F] (AR2025 p.199) Q4 FY26 carried a Rs 25.7 cr monetary loss. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

5. Execution timelines keep slipping. Sangli was guided for June 2026 [MC] (CALL Nov 2025), then July-August [MC] (CALL May 2026), and was still awaiting statutory approvals in August with about 60 customer audits to follow. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

6. Reported and management numbers do not match. FY26 EBITDA is Rs 178 cr (19%) in our statements data versus Rs 236 cr (23.5%) per the CFO. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL May 2026) Q1 FY27 revenue is Rs 233 cr versus Rs 256.4 cr. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
7. Customer concentration is high. Customers above 10% of revenue were 40% of FY25 consolidated revenue. [F] (AR2025 p.211)

8. Acquisitions carry stretched-management risk. Mehru (Mar 2025), Sukrut (50% JV, FY26), Winwin (closed SEZ insulator plant, pending), a possible Turkish Mehru plant and a US entry are all in progress at once. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)
9. A fresh equity raise is pending. Management cited 'less than INR 500 crores', and an EGM is set for 19 October 2026. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS)

10. Turkey exposure brings hyperinflation accounting (Ind AS 29), near-zero tax that depends on local R&D incentives, and geopolitical sensitivity, which management acknowledges is a P&L concern. [F] (AR2025 p.174) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [MC] (CALL May 2026)

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus narrative treats QPEEL as a scarce listed HVDC play. The documents describe something different: a holding company whose profit pool sits mostly in a 51%-owned Turkish power-electronics subsidiary. Its reported margins swing with Ind AS 29 entries. Its standalone coil business, the actual HVDC exposure, was about Rs 150-250 cr of revenue (FY25 standalone Rs 152.4 cr [F] (AR2025 p.31); FY26 QP about Rs 246 cr [MC] (CALL May 2026)). The scarcity of the qualification is plausible. But the stock trades at 12.3x TTM EV/sales [F] (NUMBERS), and that multiple asks the market to capitalise a capacity ramp that has not started. **Our variant view is that per-share attributable earnings, cash conversion and Sangli audit progress matter more than the order book headline. On all three, the evidence is weaker than the narrative.**

summary.one_line: Quality Power has a genuine, approval-gated niche in HVDC/FACTS components and a fast-growing order book, but at Rs 1,585 every DCF scenario value sits 77-93% below the price and imply 87.8% annual sales growth, while minorities share the profits, cash conversion is weak and management's figures diverge from reported ones.

[MC] The company claims to be India's only maker of HVDC/FACTS coil products above 220kV, with standalone coil EBITDA margins of 25-34%. (AR2025 p.6) (CALL Feb 2026)
[MC] The new Sangli plant (about 320,000 sq ft, 'nearly nine-fold' capacity) has a stated peak revenue of Rs 1,500-1,800 cr. (AR2025 p.6) (CALL Aug 2026)
[F] The balance sheet is net cash: borrowings Rs 40 cr, debt/equity 0.07, ROCE 32% in FY26. (NUMBERS)
[F] FY26 revenue of Rs 947 cr beat the original Rs 700-800 cr guidance; Q1 FY27 sales grew 31.6% YoY. (NUMBERS) (CALL Nov 2025)
bear_points: [F] The reverse DCF requires 87.8% sales CAGR for five years against a base-case equivalent of 19.8%; bear, base and bull values are Rs 118.5, Rs 237.6 and Rs 356.4 against a Rs 1,585 price. (NUMBERS)
[F] Endoks and Mehru are 51%-owned; NCI took Rs 34.0 cr of Rs 100.1 cr FY25 PAT, so the 62.9x P/E on total PAT understates the per-share multiple. (AR2025 p.171) (AR2025 p.166) (NUMBERS)
[F] CFO/PAT was 0.43 in FY26 and 0.55 over three years; FY26 FCF was -Rs 31 cr; other income was 27% of PBT. (NUMBERS)

[MC] FY26 EBITDA per management was Rs 236 cr (23.5%) vs Rs 178 cr (19%) in the statements data. The figures are not reconciled, and an analyst-cited correction to Q1 FY26 profit attributable to owners went unanswered. (CALL May 2026) (CALL Nov 2025) (NUMBERS)

[MC] Sangli has slipped from June 2026 to trial production pending statutory approvals, with about 60 customer audits taking about six months still to come; an equity raise below Rs 500 cr is pending. (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Aug 2026)
watch_points: Q2 FY27 results: reported EBITDA margin vs management's figure, and the Ind AS 29 monetary loss (trading window closed 1 Oct 2026; results date not disclosed). (ANNOUNCEMENTS)
Sangli: statutory approvals, trial production, and the number of customer audits completed (Hitachi, Adani, Power Grid first). (CALL Aug 2026)
19 Oct 2026 EGM: size, pricing and stated use of the fund-raise. (ANNOUNCEMENTS) (CALL Aug 2026)
Order book by entity and implied inflow vs the Rs 1,945 cr June 2026 level. (CALL Aug 2026)
Half-year cash flow: CFO/PAT and debtor days (93 at FY26) vs management's 45-60 day claim. (NUMBERS) (CALL Feb 2026)
guidance: FY27 revenue growth about 20%; 'we'll stick our guns to it', with a possible revision at Q3. (CALL Aug 2026)
EBITDA margin: 'Please model us at 20% or high teens EBITDA'; standalone about 20% achievable. (CALL Aug 2026)

Coil products: stable margin guidance about 20%; booked orders above 25%; aluminium spike may hit Q3 FY27; temporary moderation in standalone margins, particularly Q3, normalising over about 15 months as Sangli utilisation rises. (CALL Aug 2026)
Mehru EBITDA margin guidance revised to about 18% (from 15%). (CALL Aug 2026)
Endoks: legacy lines about 25%; blended margin with BESS to be indicated at Q3. (CALL Aug 2026)
Order book Rs 1,945 cr (Endoks Rs 801 cr, Mehru Rs 585 cr, QP Rs 553 cr), slated for completion in about 15 months. (CALL Aug 2026)
FY28 revenue growth guidance of 50%. (CALL Aug 2026)

Sangli: trial production targeted in August 2026 subject to approvals; about 60 audits over about 6 months; revenue 'trickling' in Q3 and a turnaround in Q4; peak about Rs 1,500-1,800 cr. (CALL Aug 2026)
HVDC CTC magnet wire: about three months of trials; full production by Q4 FY27; about Rs 500 cr of aluminium wire within 2-3 years. (CALL Aug 2026)
Endoks PCS facility operations in Q3 FY27; peak potential USD 70-80m; about USD 60m in pipeline plus USD 40m more expected in 12 months; BESS in India by end of next year. (CALL Aug 2026)

Winwin: EV about Rs 315 cr; consolidation from Q4 FY27; Rs 250-300 cr revenue without capex and Rs 450-500 cr with; Rs 50 cr capex; about Rs 200 cr of orders targeted in 9 months; margins 15-25%, stabilising in about four quarters. (CALL Aug 2026)
Fund-raise: 'less than INR 500 crores' for the Winwin closing, Winwin capex and US entry; roadshows from 20 August. (CALL Aug 2026)
GIS: plant ready this quarter; 220kV first, 400/765kV within about a year; grading-capacitor type-test slots awaited. (CALL Aug 2026)
Depreciation to rise as the Sangli CTC and Endoks PCS facilities are capitalised; interim dividend Rs 0.25 per share. (CALL Aug 2026)
